title: UPI for International Merchants: Checkout, Refunds and Settlement
summary: Set up UPI checkout for your international business. Compare Intent and QR flows, verify payments, manage refunds and reconcile overseas settlements.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


To accept UPI payments as a foreign company, you need a supported cross-border collection arrangement. Once that is approved, the practical work begins: choosing the right checkout flow, confirming whether a customer has paid, handling refunds and matching INR collections to overseas settlements.


These steps matter because a customer approving a UPI payment, your order being marked paid and money reaching your overseas bank account are different events. Your checkout and operations team need to recognise each one.


This guide explains how to implement UPI for international merchants selling online to customers in India, from the first app handoff to the final settlement record.


### Key Takeaways


- Confirm that UPI and the required checkout flows are enabled for your overseas merchant account.
- Use supported Intent flows for mobile payments and order-specific QR checkout where appropriate.
- Confirm payment through trusted server-side records. App returns and screenshots alone do not establish success.
- Track payment, transaction verification, refunds and overseas settlement separately.


##


What to Confirm Before You Enable UPI


Eligible foreign businesses can accept UPI without an Indian entity through a provider that supports the relevant cross-border collection arrangement. If you are still deciding on that route, the guide to[accepting payments from Indian customers without a local entity](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-accept-payments-from-indian-customers-without-a-local-entity/) covers the broader setup.


For this implementation, obtain confirmation of four things before development starts:


- **Account activation:** UPI is approved for your legal entity, business category and cross-border account.
- **Checkout availability:** The supported mobile, desktop, hosted-checkout or app integration is identified.
- **Operational requirements:** Your team knows which buyer, invoice and transaction details must be submitted for verification.
- **Commercial terms:** Processing fees, FX conversion, settlement timing and refund handling are documented.


A domestic UPI feature advertised by a provider is not automatically available to every foreign merchant. Confirm the specific integration and account configuration you will use. Tax obligations remain separate from payment onboarding.


##


Choose the Right UPI Checkout Flow for Each Device


The customer should be able to pay from the device they are already using. A QR-only experience can be awkward on a phone, while a desktop shopper can conveniently scan a code using a separate mobile device.


**Customer environment** **Flow to evaluate** **What to test**


Mobile browser Supported UPI Intent or app-launch flow The installed payment app opens with the correct amount, and the customer can return to checkout.


Mobile app Provider-supported mobile SDK or Intent integration App handoff, cancellation, return handling and payment-status refresh work on supported devices.


Desktop browser Order-specific dynamic QR The customer can scan with a supported UPI app and the desktop page updates after server-side confirmation.


A[dynamic UPI QR code](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-qr-code/) can carry the amount for an individual payment and help connect it to the order. Confirm the provider’s expiry and payment-status behaviour for your cross-border integration; a printable shop QR is a different setup.


Keep an alternative supported flow available when an app cannot open. Test Android and iOS separately rather than assuming the same browser behaviour. If your provider offers UPI Collect, confirm its current availability and eligibility for your cross-border account before building around manual UPI-ID entry.


##


Build an INR Checkout That Matches the Order


Indian customers pay through the supported UPI flow in INR. Make the final INR amount clear before they leave your checkout for their payment app, even if your main catalogue uses another currency.


Keep the order amount, payment amount and invoice record aligned. If you display a converted estimate, explain when the final payable amount is set. Avoid changing it silently between the product page, checkout and UPI app.


For example, an overseas software business might offer a one-time purchase for ₹1,500 at its India checkout. The payment request should show ₹1,500, and the backend should associate that payment with the same order. The foreign-currency amount eventually settled to the business is a separate calculation under its provider’s FX and fee terms.


Generate payment requests through the approved integration. Keep API secrets on your server, and use the SDK or hosted-checkout approach supported for your overseas merchant account.


##


Confirm UPI Payment Before Marking an Order Paid


Opening a payment app does not mean the customer paid. Returning to your website does not prove it either. A customer can cancel, lose connectivity or close the app while the final result is still being updated.


Use the provider’s payment-status API and authenticated events to update the order. Check that the successful payment belongs to the expected order and matches the amount and currency.


For Cashfree integrations,[webhook signature verification](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/online/webhooks/signature-verification) helps establish that an event came from Cashfree. Your system should also follow[webhook idempotency practices](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/online/webhooks/webhook-indempotency) , so repeated delivery of the same event does not trigger duplicate fulfilment.


**Keep these three checks separate:**


**Check** **What it establishes** **Operational action**


Payment status Whether the customer’s payment succeeded, failed or remains unresolved Update the order using verified payment records.


Cross-border transaction verification Whether the required buyer and transaction information has been reviewed Resolve missing information and apply the provider’s requirements for that order.


Overseas settlement status Whether the proceeds have been settled to the overseas account Match the settlement record with the bank credit.


Cashfree’s[transaction verification guidance](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/international-payments/collect-from-india/transaction-verification) describes verification states such as **Action Required** , **In Review** and **Verified** . These are verification states, not substitutes for the payment status.


Define fulfilment rules using confirmed payment information and any applicable verification conditions. Your customer-facing order page should not describe a successful payment as failed simply because the overseas settlement has not happened yet.


##


Handle UPI Failures Without Creating a Second Charge


A[UPI payment gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-payment-gateway/) for foreign businesses should give your team a recovery path for the situations below. The next step should depend on the actual payment record.


### The UPI app does not open


Check whether the device, browser and selected app are supported. Offer another enabled app-launch option or a supported QR flow. Avoid making the customer repeatedly press Pay while your system creates new payment requests.


### The customer was debited, but checkout is waiting


Keep the order in a clearly explained pending state while you retrieve the latest status. Do not immediately tell the customer to pay again. A delayed response or missing redirect can leave checkout behind the actual bank result.


The customer’s payment reference can help support investigate, but a screenshot alone should not mark the order paid. Your team needs a matching provider or bank record. The guide to[checkout payment errors](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/common-checkout-payment-errors-causes-and-fixes/) explains why pending, failed and timed-out outcomes need different handling.


### The QR code or payment session expires


Apply the provider’s expiry rules. If a fresh request is needed, first check the old attempt’s final status and associate the new attempt with the same commercial order. Make any revised amount clear before the customer approves it.


### The same event arrives more than once


Recognise the event and payment identifiers your provider supplies, and process the business action once. A repeated success notification must not issue a second licence, duplicate a booking or ship another order.


##


Refund a UPI Payment Through Its Original Transaction


Design refunds before launch, including cancellations after a payment has succeeded. Your support team should be able to locate the order, identify the original payment and initiate the approved refund process.


Use the provider’s refund facility against that payment. Sending an unrelated transfer to a UPI ID supplied in a support message can break the audit trail and create a second-payment risk if the original transaction is also refunded.


Track the refund reference, amount and status. In Cashfree’s[refund-status guidance](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/help/end-customer/refunds) , a successfully processed refund can still take additional time to appear in the customer’s account. Explain that distinction in your support messages rather than promising immediate credit.


Your support team must never ask for the customer’s UPI PIN.[NPCI’s fraud-awareness guidance](https://www.npci.org.in/fraud-awareness) explains that entering a UPI PIN authorises payment; it is not required to receive money.


##


Treat UPI AutoPay as a Separate Subscription Setup


A successful one-time UPI payment does not authorise future subscription debits. If recurring billing is part of your product, confirm that[UPI AutoPay](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-autopay/) is supported for your cross-border account, merchant category and integration.


Test mandate creation, the customer’s authorisation, recurring collection and cancellation as separate events. Record the mandate state alongside the payment state, and provide a clear customer route for managing the subscription. Do not treat an initial payment or a pending mandate as permission for every future charge.


##


Reconcile UPI Collections with Overseas Settlements


Your reconciliation process needs to connect the INR order, the customer’s UPI payment and the foreign-currency bank credit. They may have different identifiers and occur at different times.


Keep the following records connected:


- **Order:** The invoice or order number, final INR amount and relevant customer information.
- **Payment:** The provider’s payment reference, confirmed status, refunds and adjustments.
- **Settlement:** The settlement reference, conversion rate, applicable fees, settlement currency and overseas bank credit.


Under the[RBI’s Payment Aggregator Directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896) , onward settlement to overseas sellers uses the applicable Outward Collection Account arrangement. The customer’s UPI debit is not itself a direct UPI credit to your foreign bank account.


For Cashfree, the import settlement lookup helps teams retrieve settlement information associated with an order. Use the product’s reporting and bank records to investigate differences instead of comparing the foreign bank credit directly with the gross INR order total.


Agree how fees, FX conversion, refunds, verification holds and settlement cut-offs appear in reports. A confirmed UPI payment can be waiting for verification or settlement without being a failed customer payment.


##


UPI Launch Checklist for an Overseas Business


Before you accept UPI from Indian customers in production, check that:


- UPI is active on the approved cross-border merchant account.
- The supported mobile Intent and desktop QR flows work on your target devices.
- The INR amount agrees across checkout, the payment request and the order record.
- Success, failure, cancellation, expiry and pending outcomes show accurate messages.
- Webhook authentication and duplicate-event handling have been tested.
- Transaction verification information can be submitted and missing details can be resolved.
- Refunds can be initiated, tracked and explained to customers.
- Finance can match a payment to its overseas settlement and bank credit.


Test through the provider’s supported sandbox and production-validation process. A successful sandbox test checks your integration; it does not establish that every live bank, app, device or buyer will behave identically.

The implementation goal is a reliable UPI journey: the customer sees the right INR amount, the merchant confirms the payment correctly, and operations can trace refunds and settlement without losing the original order reference.

FAQs


#### Can a foreign business put a personal UPI QR code on its website?


Use the merchant payment flow supplied for your approved cross-border account. A personal QR or another party’s UPI ID does not replace overseas merchant onboarding, transaction verification or the required settlement arrangement.


#### Can customers pay by UPI while shopping on a desktop?


Yes, where the provider supports desktop QR checkout for your account. The customer scans the order-specific code using an eligible mobile UPI app, and the desktop order updates when the payment is confirmed.


#### Should I fulfil an order when a customer sends a UPI screenshot?


Confirm the payment in your provider’s server-side record first. Match it to the order and amount, and apply any required verification checks. A screenshot is useful for investigation but is not sufficient proof on its own.


#### Does one UPI payment let me charge the customer again next month?


No. Recurring collection needs the appropriate authorised mandate and a supported subscription setup. A one-time payment does not grant continuing debit permission.


#### Does domestic zero-MDR UPI pricing mean free overseas settlement?


No. Obtain the commercial terms for the cross-border service. Payment processing, currency conversion, refunds and settlement can have separate costs even where the underlying domestic UPI pricing is zero MDR.
